### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/docs/MCP_GUIDE.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/ai/index.mdx`  _(via azure_openai (literal, a string literal in AIModelConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via support_agent (literal, a string literal in fixture))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object agentModelProviderRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object agentModelProviderRemoved))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/docs/MCP_GUIDE.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0a464e68ec78fbf141cea399c1474829a99f2b28` — the merge of head `a610db7a0b656eba611b617cc84209e2908374db` into base `44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0a464e68ec78fbf141cea399c1474829a99f2b28 && git checkout 0a464e68ec78fbf141cea399c1474829a99f2b28
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797 a610db7a0b656eba611b617cc84209e2908374db && git checkout -B drift-repro 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797 && git merge --no-ff a610db7a0b656eba611b617cc84209e2908374db

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- Type surface: `Agent['model']['provider']` takes the tombstone mark, so a typed source that writes any value, `openai` included, fails `tsc`. Right.

It is the residue stage's preprocess pipe with a read-through `shape`, so `.extend()`, `.pick()`, `.omit()` and `.partial()` are gone from it. The changeset does not name this; that sentence is the lane seat's prose read.
- Authorable surface: `ai/AIModelConfig:provider` becomes a `[RETIRED]` row and is the first entry of `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[19]`, spelled as the surface file spells it. Right.
- Chain: step 19 gains `agent-model-provider-removed` at order 2. Its collection (`agents`) is disjoint from the order-1 entry's (`permissions`), so the order carries no meaning and none is needed. Right.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) is right: the accept set shrinks and nothing widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Residue stage (the dev's small call): accepted. The discriminator the tree states (`18.integration__Connector__connectionTimeoutMs.ts`) is whether a released toolchain materialized the default into something later re-parsed. It did: every 18.x parse of a `model` block wrote `provider: 'openai'`, and the metadata write door parses with the current schema and replays no conversion, so without the stage an agent exported from 18.x is refused over a value nobody typed. The silence is ruled, not chosen here (the helper's own docblock). It is bounded by `===` on one captured literal, and the pin holds `OpenAI` and a padded spelling to the refusal. A warning would need provenance JSON does not carry.
- Overlap with #37676 (still open): accepted as stated. Both insert at the head of `MAJOR_19_CONVERSIONS`; the second lander keeps both lines in identifier order.
- Absence walk excludes `ui/`: checked by reading. On `main`, six `ui/` files author the shape and all six are in this diff. The one authoring left under `ui/` is the stale-draft fixture in `AgentPreview.test.tsx`, which is there on purpose. Outside the walk's roots, `docs/notes/crm-development-standards.mdx` authored it and is cleaned here; `.claude/`, `.github/` and `examples/` hold none, and the archived 2026-06 audit under `docs/audits/` is history. The preview pill was the only reader of `model.provider` in `packages/`, `ui/` and the examples; the agent list column reads `model.model`.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #37796`: true. The card is open, `domain:skills`, `Blocked-by: #37783`, and names the table row and the eval. No marked skill example authors the key and the tombstone keeps the identifier in `packages/`, so the retirement lands first, as the playbook orders it. The row sits at `SKILL.md:369` on `main`, not 370, and the same eval's `must_contain` list also names `provider`.
- `Fixes #37712`: right. The card asks for enforce or remove, and this removes.
- `model.topP` (dev flag, out of scope): escalated to the seat. The ledger row still reads `topP DEAD`, and a search of this repository's open issues finds no card for it. It needs a carrier card where its reader would live.
- Cloud, two things this review could not read, escalated to the seat. First, the prescription says the deployment resolves a model name among the providers it has turned on; that is objectstack-ai/cloud#5055 phase 1 and must be true by the release that carries this tombstone. Second, no producer census was taken in cloud: a built-in agent there that writes `model.provider` fails `tsc` or the parse on the pin bump, which is audible, but it belongs in the bump's plan.
- `open_questions`: none stated.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, id materialisation or in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — the agent's own wrong-layer guidance still prescribes the retired key.** `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`, line 371 at this head (line 330 on `main`), inside `AgentSchema`'s `guidance`:

Followed with `anthropic`, it earns a second refusal. Followed with `openai` in untyped JSON or YAML, it is accepted and stripped in silence, so the schema's own fix sentence leads to the declared-but-unenforced state the card was filed to remove.
